day_phrase: the day appointed in this person's state (the states vote between Friday, 1 November and Wednesday, 4 December)

descriptors.R: nominee of the party that won the 1840 election and holds the Senate, which broke with the sitting President in 1841; a long-serving senator and former Secretary of State who stands for a protective tariff, a sound national currency and against annexing Texas now
descriptors.D: nominee of the party that held the presidency from 1829 to 1841 and now holds the House; a former Speaker of the House and governor, pledged to annex Texas and claim all of Oregon

compile_desc.R: the party that won the 1840 election and broke with the sitting President
compile_desc.D: the party that held the presidency from 1829 to 1841

others_line: Other candidates on some ballots, including the nominee of a small antislavery party (answer "other").
never_name: Clay, Polk, Dallas, Frelinghuysen, Birney, Tyler, Van Buren, Calhoun or Jackson

slice_sources.men: 1840 census interpolated toward 1850 to November 1844, free white men 20+ outside the eleven later-Confederate states; property tests had largely gone (Rhode Island's freehold test was relaxed for native-born men in 1843) and a few New England states let free Black men vote; calibrated to certified returns.
slice_sources.women: No women could vote for president in 1844; women 20+ (1840 census interpolated to 1844) are shown for population only.
slice_sources.south-white: 1840 census interpolated to 1844, free white adults in the eleven later-Confederate states; white men voted except in South Carolina, whose legislature chose its electors; calibrated to certified returns.
slice_sources.black-south: 1840 census interpolated to 1844, Black adults in the eleven later-Confederate states, overwhelmingly enslaved; enslaved people could not vote and no Southern state let free Black men vote.
slice_sources.immigrants: Estimate only: nativity was first recorded in 1850, so the foreign-born count is back-projected from the 1850 census and arrival records; naturalized men could vote, aliens could not.
